newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-VICTORIOUS NEW ZEALAND END LONG WAIT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-VICTORIOUS NEW ZEALAND END LONG WAIT.

text.p: New Zealand outplayed Pakistan to win the first cricket test by 44 runs with a day to spare on Sunday, taking a 1-0 lead in the two-test series.

The victory 25 minutes after tea on the fourth day was New Zealand's first on Pakistani soil since the 1968-69 tour when Graham Dowling's side won by five wickets at the same venue, Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium.
Pakistan, chasing a victory target of 276, fought well, taking the game right into the final session after resuming their second innings in a perilous state of 46 for five.

They were eventually bowled out for 231 with debutant middle-order batsman Mohammad Wasim making an unbeaten 109. He became the fourth Pakistani after Khalid Ibadullah, Javed Miandad and Salim Malik to hit a century in his maiden test, but it was to no avail.
Paceman Simon Doull, who claimed three for 39 for a match haul of eight for 85, was voted man of the match.
New Zealand made 155 and 311, and Pakistan replied with 191 and 231.
Wasim, 19, batted with great poise and assurance after starting the day at nought with Salim Malik, who was on 15.

The start of play was delayed by 55 minutes because of overnight dew on areas in the vicinity of the pitch, but this did not prevent the Kiwis from an early success when Doull snared Malik after he had made 21 with total at 60.

Wasim was then joined by Moin Khan, the top scorer in the first innings, and both batted with great determination to take the score to 135, adding precious 75 runs in 24.1 overs for the seventh wicket.
Pakistan, who were 94 for six at lunch, lost Moin in the afternoon period when he became Nathan Astle's first test victim after making 38.
The Pakistan wicketkeeper, who hit eight fours in his fluent knock, gave Lee Germon his second catch behind the stumps.
Pakistan's total was given further impetus when Wasim was joined by Mushtaq Ahmad, and they flourished in the eighth wicket partnership of 76 in 18 overs.
Wasim was in a dominant role, driving beautifully on the front foot and equally strong on the leg side.
He lost Mushtaq just before tea when the leg-spinner pushed forward to Dipak Patel to be taken by Stephen Fleming at silly point for 15.
The teenager, who was 96 at tea, eventually reached his well deserved century by turning Patel towards the fine leg boundary for his 16th four.
Altogether he batted for 232 minutes, facing 165 balls and hitting 17 fours.
Off-spinner Patel, claiming four for 36, signalled New Zealand's remarkable success by accounting for last man Shahid Nazir whose lofted drive was well taken by Chris Harris at mid-off.
"It is indeed a great day for us," said jubilant New Zealand captain Germon, adding that the team had to overcome injuries to key players.
"I am very pleased with the performance of my players. Patience was the key word in our success. We wanted to finish the match quickly but allowed the batsmen to make mistakes."
Pakistan coach Mushtaq Mohammad said he was naturally disappointed at the result but felt the absence of skipper Wasim Akram because of a shoulder pain made a lot of difference.
"Our batting was not up to the mark, barring of course Mohammad Wasim who batted with great fluency and showed that he has great potential."
The two teams meet in the second and final test at Rawalpindi from November 28. Pakistan will be without Akram, who has been ruled out of the series because of his shoulder.
